author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The first confirmed U.S. horse case of New World screwworm has been detected in Presidio County, Texas, near the Mexican border, according to federal and state animal-health information reported by Reuters. The parasite's larvae feed on living tissue and can spread quickly through livestock and wildlife if wounds are not identified and treated.

The Texas Animal Health Commission restricted movement of warm-blooded animals from an infested zone covering parts of Presidio and Jeff Davis counties. The U.S. Equestrian Federation said the case involved a working ranch horse with an infestation in a hind limb. Officials had not established the animal's origin in the initial report.

The United States eradicated a major screwworm outbreak in the 1960s after thousands of livestock deaths. Experts estimate that a widespread return could create as much as $1.8 billion in economic damage. Animal-health authorities are urging owners to inspect animals regularly, treat wounds promptly, control flies and strengthen biosecurity. The confirmed horse infection is a developing agricultural-health event, and authorities have not announced evidence of broader U.S. transmission from this case.
dek: Animal-health authorities restricted movement in parts of two Texas counties after confirming the flesh-eating parasite in a working ranch horse.
headline: First U.S. horse case of New World screwworm confirmed in Texas
